context: The prompt asks to remove the 'File Path (relative to .rdd-instance):' section with its file selector from the Web UI. This section is currently part of the Files tab and includes a text input field and Load File button. We need to clarify the scope and impact of this removal.

questions.question-text: Should the entire File Browser card be removed, or only the file path input section?

options.label: Remove only the file path input field and Load File button (lines 331-338 in index.html)
options.pros: Preserves the file editor functionality and quick access buttons, allows users to still edit files through quick access
options.cons: Users cannot manually enter custom file paths anymore, limited to predefined quick access files

options.label: Remove the entire File Browser card including file editor and quick access buttons
options.pros: Completely eliminates the manual file editing capability from Web UI, enforces workflow through domain-specific pages
options.cons: Removes useful functionality for advanced users, may make debugging harder

options.label: Keep quick access buttons but remove the manual file path input field
options.pros: Provides guided access to common files while preventing arbitrary file access, balance between control and usability
options.cons: More selective removal requires more careful code changes

questions.recommendation-rationale: Removing only the manual file path input section (option A) is recommended because it addresses the prompt's request precisely while preserving the file editor and quick access buttons. This maintains useful functionality for editing common files through the predefined buttons while removing the arbitrary path input capability.

questions.question-text: Should the Files tab be removed from the navigation menu?

options.label: Yes, remove the Files tab completely from navigation
options.pros: Cleaner navigation menu, enforces use of domain-specific pages for file management
options.cons: Removes access to file editor functionality, may require users to edit files externally

options.label: No, keep the Files tab with the remaining functionality
options.pros: Maintains access to file editor and quick access functionality if we keep those features
options.cons: Tab might be nearly empty if most content is removed

questions.recommendation-rationale: Keeping the Files tab is recommended if we preserve the file editor and quick access buttons (as suggested in Q1 option A). This allows users to continue accessing and editing common files through the predefined quick access buttons, which is a useful capability that complements the domain-specific pages.

questions.question-text: Should the loadFile() and loadFileQuick() JavaScript functions be modified or removed?

options.label: Keep both functions to support quick access buttons functionality
options.pros: Allows quick access buttons to continue working, maintains file viewing/editing capability for predefined files
options.cons: Keeps code that might not be used if file browser is completely removed

options.label: Remove loadFile() but keep loadFileQuick() for quick access buttons
options.pros: Removes manual file loading while preserving quick access, cleaner separation of concerns

options.label: Remove both functions completely
options.pros: Complete cleanup of file loading functionality, enforces domain-specific file access patterns
options.cons: Removes file editing capability entirely, may force users to external editors

questions.recommendation-rationale: Removing loadFile() but keeping loadFileQuick() aligns with removing the manual path input while preserving quick access button functionality. This provides a clean separation where users can access predefined important files (registry, requirements, technical design) but cannot arbitrarily browse the file system.
